table_title: For each of the thirteen Olympian deities enumerated in the List section of Wikipedia's 'Twelve Olympians' article — the article notes there is no single canonical list of the Twelve and that Hestia and Dionysus are commonly swapped — give the deity's Roman equivalent, the primary domain (sphere of influence) the deity is most associated with, and the deity's most iconic symbol per the master-article foregrounding.
db_analog: SELECT g.greek_name AS greek_deity, g.roman_equivalent, g.primary_domain, g.primary_symbol FROM greek_deities g WHERE g.is_olympian = TRUE ORDER BY g.greek_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'Twelve Olympians' master article + 13 per-deity Wikipedia articles, all accessed 2026-05-13. The universe is the 13 Olympians enumerated in the master article's 'List' section. The article explicitly states 'there is no single canonical list of the twelve Olympian gods' and that Hestia and Dionysus are commonly swapped; the article's enumerated table itself includes both, which the staged set follows. Apollo is uniquely the Olympian whose Roman equivalent retains the Greek name (his per-deity Wikipedia article has a dedicated 'Roman Apollo' section). Dionysus's Roman equivalent is staged as 'Liber' per the master article and the Dionysus per-deity article's infobox; the more popularly-used Roman name 'Bacchus' is mentioned as Dionysus's alternate Greek name in his own infobox and is a defensible alternative answer for LLM evaluation. Hades is explicitly excluded by the master article ('his realm was far away from Olympus in the underworld, and thus he was not usually considered to be one of the Olympians'); his Roman equivalent (Dis Pater / Pluto) is therefore not staged. All facts are stable historical-mythology record.
_extraction_notes: Factual_lookup instance: tests whether the model can identify the Roman equivalent + Primary Domain + Primary Symbol for each of the 13 Olympian deities. Universe = 13 Olympians per Wikipedia 'Twelve Olympians' master article's enumerated List (Aphrodite, Apollo, Ares, Artemis, Athena, Demeter, Dionysus, Hephaestus, Hera, Hermes, Hestia, Poseidon, Zeus). Schema: 4 cols (Greek Deity PK + Roman Equivalent categorical + Primary Domain text + Primary Symbol text). Universe is source_defined: the article enumerates 13 explicitly while stating that there is no single canonical list of the Twelve (Hestia OR Dionysus is the variant swap-pair) — staging both follows the article's actual table. Apollo retains the Greek name in Roman tradition (only Olympian whose Greek and Roman names match). Dionysus → Liber per the master article (Bacchus is the popular alt name, staged as the secondary alternative). Hades is explicitly excluded by the article (not an Olympian per Wikipedia). Sort order: Greek Deity ASC (alphabetical) — natural for a 13-row factual-lookup table. NEW Religion/Mythology subdomain in Religion family (Religion extends from 1 to 2 subdomains, joining Religion/Holy Sites). NEW entity class: Greek deities (mythological figures) — no other instance is keyed by mythological figures. Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + extinctions-cycles + deserts-cycles + tennis-cycles + music-genres-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Greek Deity (Wikipedia article-title form); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles each (master + per-deity); (c) explicit selection rule for Roman Equivalent (per master article's table and per-deity article — typically the infobox 'Equivalents' field, but Apollo's same-name-in-Roman is grounded by a dedicated 'Roman Apollo' section rather than an infobox field); (d) explicit Primary Domain rule (the article-foregrounded sphere of influence per the master article's text); (e) explicit Primary Symbol rule (the article-foregrounded single most-iconic symbol per the master article); (f) source-defined universe (13 Olympians per master article's enumerated list, including Hestia AND Dionysus); (g) operation_type 'filter' (universe filtered to Olympians, excluding Hades and other deities).
